title: Choose CYCLEBOOK's visual world
question: Your steer leads: the research note, with Deere green and yellow used sparingly. Build it, pick another, or re-roll.

options.label: Initiation of Coverage, Deere-signaled
options.lineage: Sell-side initiation notes, marked up the way analysts actually read them
options.thesis: A research note on Deere where green appears only when Deere itself is speaking (guidance) and yellow is the analyst's highlighter on the one finding per page.
options.viewport: PULSE as the note's front page: DE masthead and price box, the investment view with one yellow-highlighted finding, a key-data table with guidance figures set in Deere green, and Exhibits 1 and 2 at right.
options.risk: Familiar grammar; the green and yellow have to stay rare, or the note turns into a Deere press release.

options.label: The Graphics Desk
options.thesis: Every chart is titled with its finding, labeled on the line instead of in a legend, and sourced underneath; Deere green marks the one series that matters.
options.viewport: PULSE as a markets page: the headline finding across the top, one large revenue chart with Q3 FY26 annotated on the line, three small charts beneath.
options.risk: Reads as a news article more than an analyst's instrument, and gives the MODEL LAB controls a weaker home.

options.label: The Statistical Release
options.lineage: USDA WASDE and crop production reports
options.thesis: Deere's numbers set like a government statistical release: dense fiscal-period tables, change-since-last-report columns, footnoted sources.
options.viewport: PULSE as a release page: fiscal-quarter columns and segment rows, a change-versus-prior column, and guidance revisions marked in green and yellow.
options.risk: Dense tables can feel dry to a hiring manager skimming for ten minutes; charts take a back seat.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A company-snapshot dashboard at the craft level of FactSet Company Snapshot, Koyfin and Morningstar's stock pages.
canonCard.viewport: A ticker header with price and daily change, KPI tiles, a price chart, and financial and segment tables below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like the tools a hiring manager already uses every day, so it proves craft but not a point of view.
